chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the ritual bath for Ihram, then slept before entering the state of Ihram. He said: He must repeat the ritual bath.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ع: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Musa al-Kadhim or Imam Ali al-Rida depending on context, here used as the authority
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: Does a person need to repeat their ritual bath for Ihram if they sleep before officially entering the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that sleeping after performing the ritual bath (*ghusl*) for Ihram but before the formal declaration (*talbiyah*) invalidates the purity, necessitating a repeat. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of ritual state (*muwalat*) and the intentionality required to maintain the validity of the bath until the specific act of entering Ihram is completed. It highlights the precision in Fiqh regarding the temporal link between purification and the commencement of the sacred rite.
